sections.content: How many people stayed in Shrewsbury after gaining qualifications?

Shrewsbury is a medium-sized town in the West Midlands. Shrewsbury does not have its own university.

Shrewsbury has medium levels of deprivation.

Overall, Shrewsbury ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 3,000 state-school pupils from Shrewsbury who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 940 (31%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 985 (33%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Shrewsbury to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Shrewsbury's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Shrewsbury in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Shrewsbury move to?

Of Shrewsbury's graduates, 400 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 35 of those graduates (9%) were living fairly locally, in the Shrewsbury travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Shrewsbury's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 225 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 70 of those qualified non-graduates (31%) were living fairly locally, in the Shrewsbury travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Shrewsbury's GCSE cohort:

  • 315 graduates left the West Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was the North West
  • 110 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the West Midlands
  • the most common regions they moved to were the North West and the South West

In 2018 to 2019, 35% of graduates and 26% of qualified non-graduates living in Shrewsbury had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 795 graduates and 1,005 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Shrewsbury. This is compared with the 940 graduates and 985 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 65% of the graduates had also lived in Shrewsbury as GCSE pupils, while 35% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Shrewsbury in 2018 to 2019, 74% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 26% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
